transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-05
Start: 09:30 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Chu (Redwood SE), Lena Morgan (Orion Head of ML), Carlos Diaz (SRE), Priya Shah (Product), Tom Reeves (Infra), Sofia Alvarez (Data)

Summary section (auto):
Maya: quick recap - we ran the evals you sent, looked at hallucination rates and latency. Lena: yes, thanks, saw the reports. discussed pinning to v1.3-quantized for cost but worried about small regressions. agreed to benchmarks, pricing, and VPC tests.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll kick off with a quick agenda 
results recap, model selection options, pinning and fallback plan, next steps. Ethan's gonna run through the numbers.
[00:22] Ethan: cool. so we ran the batch of 5k eval prompts you shared across three variants: v1.2-fp16, v1.3-quant, and v1.3-fp16. latency median for v1.2 was 220ms per token in our hosted runs, v1.3-fp16 is about 240, v1.3-quant is 150ms token but with a slight uptick in low-frequency factual errors on some prompts.
[00:47] Lena: sorry can you repeat the last bit on errors? was that consistent across prompt types?
[00:55] Ethan: yeah, so for knowledge-based prompts we saw a 1.8% increase in hallucination compared to v1.2, mostly on long-context lookups. For intent/slot extraction tests the quality delta was negligible.
[01:15] Priya: important for product - most of our calls are short queries so latency is weighted heavier, but for help articles we care about factual correctness.
[01:28] Carlos: network question - were these tests on Dedicated or hosted? were you using VPC peering?
[01:35] Ethan: these specific runs were in hosted, default infra, not VPC-peered. we can repeat under your VPC/Private setup to measure egress and peering overhead.
[01:50] Tom: ok yeah please do that, our infra team needs a sense for round-trip time and throughput under peering.
[02:00] Maya: on pinning: we recommend pinning the route to v1.3-quant as a canary for cost savings but with an automated fallback to v1.2-fp16 if quality regressions exceed threshold X (we'll propose thresholds).
[02:18] Lena: is that easy to reason about? can we set per-route thresholds? we want some prompts to always hit the higher-quality model.
[02:26] Ethan: yes you can create routing rules - per-route weighting, and also the eval alignment rule where the runtime checks a small percentage of responses against a golden set and if signal shows regressions it shifts traffic. we can scope that in the POC.
[02:42] Priya: how granular are those golden sets? per-skill?
[02:46] Ethan: you can do per-route or per-tag, we recommend starting per-skill, e.g., FAQs vs checkout support.
[03:00] Maya: pricing implications - v1.3-quant lowers token cost ~35% in our estimates; so big savings at scale. i'll send a dedicated pilot quote after this call.
[03:15] Lena: latency numbers for v1.3-quant look promising. what about tail latency?
[03:21] Ethan: tail is trickier - 95th percentile improved, but 99th we saw occasional spikes when KV cache misses occurred; with warmed cache on repeated prefixes it's much better.
[03:35] Sofia: that matches our production patterns - many sessions are repeat queries so cache warmups should help.
[03:40] Carlos: any known issues with quantized kernels on your Dedicated nodes? e.g. GPU oom?
[03:47] Ethan: we tested on A100 and Ampere-based hosts - quantized path reduces memory footprint, usually helps; OOMs are rarer but we noted one case with long-context + large batch where we exceeded KV cache sizing; we can tune cache allocation.
[04:05] Tom: worth a check - can you run a stress test with our worst-case batch plus long context to validate?
[04:12] Ethan: yep we'll do stress runs under your peered VPC.
[04:20] Lena: rollback behavior - we need a clean rollback if quality drops in prod. how instantaneous are rollbacks?
[04:28] Maya: rollbacks can be instant at routing level - flip the route or enable automatic fallback. there is also canary gradual ramp options.
[04:36] Priya: do we get telemetry showing the rollback reason?
[04:39] Ethan: yes, the console shows model-level metrics, diffs vs baseline, and an alert stream. we can forward those to your observability.
[04:50] Lena: timeline question - if we pin to v1.3-quant for cost, but then a patched upstream model appears, how do version upgrades work?
[05:00] Maya: we version and you can pin to exact model build (e.g., v1.3-2027-09-28). upgrades are explicit; we won't auto-upgrade without your sign-off.
[05:12] Lena: good. next, benchmarks under peering - will we see a big delta?
[05:19] Ethan: depends on your network, but usually peering adds a few ms; bigger impact is serialization or attach time if you use private deployments with extra auth checks.
[05:30] Carlos: our extra auth is mTLS, shouldn't add more than 8-10ms.
[05:35] Ethan: good to know. we'll factor that in.
[05:40] Maya: ok let's run through the explicit A/B we propose: test v1.2-fp16 (baseline), v1.3-fp16 (feature parity), v1.3-quant (cost-optimized). run 1k QPS bursts and 10k smaller queries, measure median, p95/p99, and hallucination delta on the 50-sample golden prompts.
[06:02] Priya: for product, we want a split by use-case - quick answers vs knowledge lookups.
[06:10] Ethan: noted.

[07:15] (skipping ahead to discussion about fallback mechanics)
[07:15] Ethan: also want to note automatic prefix caching will help your sessions where users ask follow-ups. quant path is compatible with our cache; just watch the initial warmups.
[07:40] Lena: any concerns about SSO/KMS with Private?
[07:45] Maya: we support SAML SSO, KMS integration, and HSM could be arranged for Private. we'll share security docs.
[07:52] Tom: can we get SOC2 and ISO attestations?
[07:55] Maya: yes, sending SOC2/ISO and our security package after meeting.

[12:40] Carlos: one more technical - how deterministic are outputs across quant vs fp16? any nondeterminism for debugging?
[12:48] Ethan: quant sometimes shaves off tiny probabilities causing token choice diffs; it's not deterministic across types, but we have logs and request replay to help debugging.

[22:05] Lena: thanks. so summary of asks: run benchmark on peered VPC, run stress test long context + worst-batch, share pricing and sample prompts.
[22:18] Maya: yep, and we'll propose threshold numbers for automatic fallback and canary ramp rates.
[22:26] Priya: timeline OK - we'll share prompts by Friday.
[22:30] Maya: sweet. any blockers?
[22:33] Tom: none on infra once peering is approved.
[22:36] Sofia: we'll attach dataset and rubric to the shared drive after this call.
[22:40] Maya: perfect. i'll follow up with the pricing doc and dedicated pilot terms.

[41:30] Maya: ok wrapping, thanks everyone. next sync same time next week unless we need to escalate.
[41:40] Lena: thanks all.
[41:45] End meeting.
